key_insight: ADAPT-SSVQE enables a single quantum simulation to extract multiple nuclear shell-model eigenstates at once while preserving fermionic and angular-momentum symmetries.
engineering_relevance: This provides a path to bypass the exponential Hilbert-space bottleneck in nuclear many-body calculations, making quantum hardware more relevant for spectroscopy-scale simulations.
method: Map the nuclear Hamiltonian to qubits with the Jordan-Wigner transformation.
Use a symmetry-preserving ADAPT ansatz with single- and double-excitation operators.
Optimize a weighted energy sum in SSVQE to converge several orthogonal states in one run.
evidence_signal: In simulation, the authors benchmarked 2 and 3 identical nucleons in a j=9/2 orbital, extracting 5 and 10 mutually orthogonal states, respectively, within a 10-qubit active space with spectroscopic accuracy versus exact diagonalization.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated in simulation on a small active space, so scaling to larger nuclei will depend on circuit depth, ansatz expressibility, and hardware noise.
paper_title: Full-Spectrum Quantum Simulation for the Nuclear Shell Model
